title: The notch plays
idea: Shelf's bookmark laid on its side, tail to the left, so the notch it already has points right as a play button. One solid shape with no holes: the play is the space the bookmark's own tail leaves open.
built: Today's bookmark turned a quarter turn clockwise, 37 dp wide (its height on the tile) and 54.8 long. The notch is deepened from 11/34 of the width to 14/18, the proportion of Shelf's in-app play icon (Lucide play: 18 tall, 14 deep), so the notch and the player's play are the same triangle. In a depth study (0.55, 0.62, 0.70, 0.78) the dark wedge read as a chevron up to 0.62 and as a play from 0.70, most firmly at 0.78. The body behind the apex is 26 dp, 0.7 of the width. Corner radii follow the bookmark: shoulders 4/34 of the width, tips 1.5/34, and the notch's apex takes the shoulder radius (4.35 dp) so the play's point is as soft as the shoulders. Centred on y 54. Horizontally the notch takes weight from the left, so the box is moved left of centre by 0.65 of the gap between its box centre and its centroid: box-centred looked right-heavy, centroid-centred pushed the tips past the safe circle. Reach 32.6 dp, inside the 33 dp circle.
small: Every size keeps the whole drawing, because there is nothing inside to drop. 48 px: 24 x 34 px, the notch 18 deep on a 2 : 3 staircase (the nearest clean slope to the play's 0.78), shoulders r 3, the apex r 3 (the master's 4.35 dp is 2.9 px here), sharp tips. 32 px: 16 x 23, notch 12, shoulders r 2, apex r 1. 16 px: 8 x 11, notch 6, shoulders r 1, sharp apex, 2 px clear on the left and 3 on the right. Each cut's body is the master's at that scale, so the mark sits where the master does. Glyph: 14 x 20 in the 20 px box, an 11 px notch (11/14, the play's ratio again) with its apex on a whole pixel.
risks: On its side the bookmark loses the hang that makes it a bookmark: it can read as a tag, a label, a pennant or the tail of an arrow first, and its square shoulders are the only cue left, small at 48 px. Gmail's 'important' marker is a horizontal tag with a notched end, and Plex's chevron sits close to the notch's outline on a dark tile. A bookmark paired with a play triangle is Google Play Books' ground, which the brief flags; here the play is empty space on a sideways shape, but the pairing is the same. The play is a figure-ground switch: some people will see a chevron bite or a forward arrow until it is pointed out. The deeper notch makes the prongs long and pointed, so it is further from today's chunky bookmark than any upright option.
